title: PowerPoint on Mac: attach and reference an image when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, licence-assignment controls and described image-reference workflow are supported. Its user-opt-in default fits the documented workflow, and its gaps are limited to image-specific controls, licensing and handling that the searches did not establish.

claims.claim: No admin switch specific to attaching and referencing images in PowerPoint Agent Mode is documented in the material found.

claims.claim: No separate administrative action to enable this image-reference feature is documented.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Licence assignment is under Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the **Users** > [Active users] page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select **Licenses and Apps**. Expand the **Licenses** section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense with the printed UserId, AddLicenses SkuId and empty RemoveLicenses assigns a licence to a user.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least a License Administrator or User Administrator role.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.where: controls[0].governs and note; Governance controls; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The licence-assignment control governs the licensed Copilot in PowerPoint experience rather than image referencing alone.
claims.quote: You **have** the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: Microsoft's Copilot requirements page says privacy controls for connected experiences can affect Copilot availability and links to those controls.
claims.quote: Review the privacy controls for connected experiences. These controls can affect the availability of Copilot features. For more information, see [Microsoft Copilot and privacy controls for connected experiences]

claims.claim: Turning off connected experiences that analyse content makes Copilot features unavailable in PowerPoint.
claims.quote:
If you turn off connected experiences that analyze your content on devices in your organization, Microsoft Copilot features won't be available to your users in the following apps:
- Excel
- OneNote
- Outlook
- PowerPoint
- Word

claims.claim: The connected-content privacy restriction applies on Mac when running the most current PowerPoint version.
claims.quote: This applies to when you're running the most current version of these apps on Windows, Mac, iOS, or Android devices.

claims.claim: Turning off all connected experiences also makes those PowerPoint Copilot features unavailable.
claims.quote: There's also a privacy control that turns off all connected experiences, including connected experiences that analyze your content. If you use that privacy control, Microsoft Copilot features won't be available in the apps and on the devices described above.

claims.claim: The Copilot release notes describe gradual deployment to a subset of tenant users before expanding across the organisation.
claims.quote: Copilot features are introduced using a safe deployment model, gradually rolling out to a subset of users within a tenant before expanding across the organization.
